title: Automated Quality Inspection for Precision Manufacturing
business: A high-precision electronics manufacturer producing micro-components.
problem: Manual visual inspection of micro-components is slow, prone to human fatigue, and results in inconsistent quality control standards across shifts.
solution: Implementing a computer vision pipeline using TensorFlow Keras to classify component images as 'pass' or 'fail' based on structural integrity, enabling real-time automated sorting.
steps: Collect and label a dataset of micro-component images categorized by defect types.
Utilize tf.keras to define a Sequential model with convolutional layers for feature extraction.
Normalize input image data to ensure consistent pixel intensity values for the model.
Compile the model using an appropriate optimizer and loss function for binary classification.
Train the model on the labeled dataset and evaluate performance against a hold-out test set.
outcome: A consistent, high-speed inspection process that reduces human error and standardizes quality thresholds across all production lines.
limitation: The model may suffer from 'concept drift' if manufacturing processes change, requiring periodic retraining; monitor this by tracking classification accuracy over time against manual audits.

code.content:
import tensorflow as tf
# Define a simple model for binary classification
model = tf.keras.models.Sequential([
  tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(128, 128)), # Input image size
  tf.keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
  tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid') # Binary output: Pass/Fail
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
